problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision exactly as posed (whether to enter, and by which route) and answers both parts. Slide 8 uses the board's own limits (ambition, $18M cap, payback, 8% margin floor) as the comparison columns for A, B and J, and slide 10 applies the one-launch bandwidth constraint to Japan. It identifies early what the answer turns on: ad cost for Amazon, sell-through at Onsoo's awareness for retail, and the fact that no route reaches $40M within the limits. Nothing material to fix.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the four summary points are the four sections, and almost every title is a claim its slide supports; the titles alone give the argument. Three flaws. The headline comparison (slides 8–9) runs Option A at 25% ACoS, an assumption the document later rejects, so 'within every financial limit' and 'generates cash from 2028 onward' rest on a case the author does not believe (at the recommended 28%, 2028 is still negative per slide 22). The ad-cost gate (29%) sits above the document's own 28.6% break-even. Planning at 28% ACoS and 25% duty together misses payback on the document's own 26.9% break-even, and this is not acknowledged. Slides 7, 13 and 14 overlap somewhat.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived the key figures and they reproduce: Amazon unit contribution $10.72 before ads and $4.005 at 28%; retail $7.55; Option A cumulative cash $2.40M / $0.38M / −$2.32M at 25% / 28% / 32% ACoS and −$3.43M in the combined downside; break-even ACoS 28.6% (26.9% at 25% duty); Option B cumulative −$9.5M / −$15.1M / −$18.9M / −$20.8M; group margin 4.5% in 2027 and below 8% through 2029; Japan cumulative $1.8M; market shares and growth. Derivations are transparent, and evidence against the recommendation is used (32% benchmark, two stalled Amazon-first peers, repeat below Korea). All critical evidence is used and the correlation memo is handled properly. Flaws: 'ad cost, not volume, decides the payback year' is asserted with no volume sensitivity, even though the document itself notes two of three Amazon-first peers stalled below $5M and the 2027 plan needs 1.8 times June's pace; the duty cash cost is given as $0.98M where the document's own model implies $1.11M; 'still selling' for Gaon Lab and Yeoreum is not in the pack; Option B is not re-run at 2.6 units per door.

strategic_judgment.rationale: Clear, defensible recommendation (Amazon-led with gates, closest to R1) that follows from the analysis. Alternatives are compared on the board's criteria, the $40M ambition is explicitly reset to about $26M, the retail trigger is raised to 20% awareness on the sell-through evidence, and labels, tariff and next steps with owners are covered. It avoids every trap. Flaws: the gate is set at 29%, above the 28.6% break-even and well above the 26.9% that applies under the 25% duty it tells the board to plan for, so the recommended settings miss payback and the document does not say so or ask the board to accept that. The only response to a failed gate is 'hold spend', with no exit or kill criterion. There is no volume or repeat-rate gate despite the stalled-peer evidence. Japan is dismissed mainly on revenue size, without confronting that it returns more cumulative cash by 2030 ($1.8M vs $0.4M at 28% ACoS) at lower risk.

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on slide 2, the language is plain and precise, and titles carry the message. Twenty-four slides including four section dividers, an appendix divider and some overlapping retail slides (7, 13, 14 repeat the TikTok and Saebom points) is somewhat longer than the decision needs, though most content slides earn their place.

unsupported_claims.quote: Ad cost, not volume, decides the payback year
unsupported_claims.why: No volume sensitivity is run. The planning-team volumes are taken as given, although the document itself notes two of three Amazon-first peers stayed below $5M and that the 2027 plan needs 1.8 times June's pace.

unsupported_claims.quote: Gaon Lab | Amazon-first, 2022 | Below $5M | Stayed small; still selling
unsupported_claims.why: The pack reports only that Gaon Lab and Yeoreum had US revenue below $5M in 2025; it does not say they are still in the market.

unsupported_claims.quote: Buyers find new brands online, not in stores
unsupported_claims.why: Overstated: 38% discovered their last new brand on TikTok against 17% in a store. Stores are a smaller discovery channel, not a non-channel.

numerical_errors.quote: $0.98M Cash cost of a duty rise to 25%, 2027–30 ($0.35 a unit × 2.81 million units)
numerical_errors.correct: About $1.11M including the higher inventory cost, as the document's own model implies (−$2.32M to −$3.43M on slide 17, and the 26.9% break-even on slide 18). $0.98M is only the per-unit duty effect.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Payback by 2030 needs advertising below 28.6% of Amazon sales, a ceiling the pilot only just meets
logical_contradictions.quote_b: Ad-cost gate: ACoS at or below 29%
logical_contradictions.why: The gate tolerates an ad cost above the document's own break-even, so the launch can pass the gate and still miss the board's payback limit.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Plan at the pilot's 28%; hold spend if it passes 29%
logical_contradictions.quote_b: Plan for 25% until the mid-2027 decision ... At 25% duty, payback needs ad cost below 27%
logical_contradictions.why: The two recommended planning settings together (28% ACoS, 25% duty) miss payback by 2030 on the document's own numbers, yet Option A is presented as the route within the board's limits.

recommendation.summary: Approve Option A (Amazon-led) in March 2027 and defer Japan. Plan at 28% ACoS with a gate at 29%, plan for 25% duty until the mid-2027 decision, launch with a US entity, MoCRA registration and English labels, add specialty retail no earlier than 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and awareness passes 20%, and reset the 2030 goal to about $26M.
recommendation.rationale: Meets all four defensibility criteria: compares A, B and J on cap, payback and margin floor; tests the 25% ACoS and 4.5 units-per-door assumptions against the benchmarks; states the break-even ACoS (28.6%, or 26.9% at 25% duty) and gates; and says no modelled route reaches $40M within the limits. Weaknesses are the gate set slightly above break-even and the lack of a kill criterion or volume/repeat gate.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: Keeps the CEO's Amazon-first route but changes five settings: ACoS planned at 28% instead of 25%, retail trigger raised from 15% to 20% awareness on the sell-through bands, label and entity fix, tariff planned at 25%, and the 2030 goal reset to about $26M. This matches the expected handling. It surfaces the contradictions in the pack (25% vs 32% ACoS, 4.5 vs 2.6 units per door, correlation vs causation, one in three Amazon-first peers scaling). The one unsupported causal claim is that ad cost rather than volume decides payback, made without a volume sensitivity.

output.overall_comment: Strong, numerically sound document. Every key figure I re-derived matches the pack and the answer key, including the Option A sensitivity, the 28.6% break-even, the Option B cash path and the group margin check. It keeps the CEO's hypothesis with well-reasoned conditions, dismantles the retail-led case on both sell-through and the correlation memo, and resets the $40M ambition honestly. The main weaknesses are in gate design and consistency: the 29% ACoS gate sits above the document's own break-even; the recommended planning settings (28% ACoS, 25% duty) jointly miss payback without that being flagged; there is no volume or repeat gate or exit criterion despite the stalled-peer evidence; and the headline comparison runs on the 25% ACoS that the document later rejects. Japan is fairly presented but dismissed mainly on revenue size. Somewhat longer than needed. Weighted score 4.15.
